headline: GOLD BOUNCES $10.80 TO $4,284 SATURDAY MORNING — October Hike Bets Plateau Near 70%; Monthly Loss Holds at 6.5%; Silver Recovers Toward $64
snippet: Gold spot opened at $4,284.20 per troy ounce Saturday September 26, up $10.80 from Friday's close, as CME FedWatch rate-hike odds for October stabilized near 70% following three days of upward pressure that had erased virtually all of gold's 2026 gains. Silver recovered toward $64 per ounce on the same session. The modest bounce ends a seven-session losing streak but leaves gold roughly 24% below its January $5,595 record and on track for its worst monthly performance of 2026, down approximately 6.5% month-to-date. The pause in hike-expectations movement is allowing some technical buyers to re-engage at the lower end of the post-September-FOMC range, though the 150-day moving average remains declining and the metal continues to print lower highs and lower lows since the January peak.

headline: CAMBRIA GOLD HITS 166 g/t AU + 3,383 g/t AG OVER 3.1m AT PREMIER BC — Bonanza Result in Canada's Silver Capital; Program Expands to 42,000m
snippet: Cambria Gold Mines (TSXV: CAMB) drilled bonanza-grade precious metals at the Premier Mine Complex near Stewart in northwestern BC, with highlight hole P26U-0095 returning 166.22 g/t gold and 3,383 g/t silver over 3.1 metres — including an ultra-high-grade core of 467 g/t gold and 9,510 g/t silver over 1.1 metres — the strongest result in the 2026 infill campaign. Additional significant intervals include 37.38 g/t Au over 5.0 metres and 18.26 g/t Au over 9.2 metres across a total of 6,923 metres from 70 surface and underground holes. Cambria also announced an expansion of the Premier infill program from 30,000 to 42,000 planned metres to include the Big Missouri and Silver Coin deposits, positioning the project for a materially larger resource in one of North America's historically highest-grade gold-silver corridors.

headline: COPPER AT $6.61, ZINC -1.8% ON SATURDAY — Escondida Stays Shut; Strike Vote Starts Monday; Chinese Galvanizing Demand Stays Weak
snippet: COMEX copper held near $6.61 per pound Saturday September 26 as the dollar's two-month high continued to weigh on the metals complex while BHP's Escondida copper mine in Chile remained shut following the September 23 worker fatality. Sindicato No. 2's strike vote runs September 28-30 with union leadership urging members to reject BHP's final offer; a rejected contract triggers a mandatory five-day government mediation period before a legal strike can begin — overlaying a potential labour stoppage on an already production-constrained site. Zinc fell 1.8% to approximately $3,905 per tonne on continued soft Chinese galvanising demand with no positive catalyst from construction activity. Senior copper miners Southern Copper and Freeport-McMoRan posted minor gains Friday, suggesting equity markets are partially looking through near-term futures weakness to the structural supply deficit thesis.

headline: GLENCORE FOUNDING PARTNER IN $12B US CRITICAL MINERALS RESERVE — $500M EXIM Loan; All 60 USGS Critical Minerals Targeted; 2,000t Cobalt Pre-Positioned
snippet: The US Export-Import Bank named Glencore and trading firm Mercuria as founding partners in VaultCo, a government-backed public-private partnership to build a US strategic critical minerals reserve, with the announcement made September 23 and Glencore receiving a $500 million EXIM commitment. The $12 billion programme is designed to cover all 60 minerals on the USGS critical minerals list, combining EXIM's financing capacity with Glencore's global supply procurement networks. Glencore had already pre-positioned approximately 2,000 tonnes of cobalt valued at $115 million in anticipation of the programme, demonstrating the depth of its readiness. For junior mining investors, VaultCo represents a structural demand floor for critical minerals — a US government bid for physical metal that could underpin prices during commodity market softness and signals that industrial policy is now a direct factor in critical mineral valuations.

headline: USA RARE EARTH NAMES THRAS MORAITIS CEO AS HUMPTON RETIRES OCT 1 — Serra Verde Merger Completes Full-Stack US Critical Mineral Supply Chain
snippet: USA Rare Earth (NASDAQ: USAR) announced that CEO Barbara Humpton will retire effective October 1, 2026, with Thrasyvoulos (Thras) Moraitis — currently CEO of the Serra Verde Group — named as her successor, and Michael Blitzer appointed Executive Chair immediately. The transition accompanies USA Rare Earth's combination with Serra Verde, one of the only companies outside China operating a fully integrated rare earth mine, processing plant and oxide separation circuit. The combined entity is designed to supply the entire US rare earth value chain from mine to separated oxide for defence and clean energy manufacturers. Moraitis's operational track record at Serra Verde in Brazil is expected to accelerate completion of USA Rare Earth's Round Top mine in Texas and its in-house separation facility — closing the vertical integration gap that has hampered Western rare earth independence for years.

headline: GREENLAND SECURITY PACT RESHAPES RARE EARTH RACE — CRITICAL METALS TANBREEZ PERMIT SURGED 25% BEFORE 6% GIVEBACK; ARCTIC HURDLES PERSIST
snippet: A US-Denmark security pact granting permanent US security control over Greenland triggered sharp moves in rare earth equities last week, with Critical Metals (NASDAQ: CRML) surging as much as 43% intraday before settling at a 25% weekly gain and then pulling back 6% on profit-taking. Critical Metals holds the Tanbreez permit, Greenland's only active rare earth exploitation licence, which covers the world's largest rare earth deposit by in-situ value. Analysts note the security pact grants no new mining rights or capital and the agreement text remains unpublished — leaving the premium tied to geopolitical sentiment. The US is separately backing a pipeline of African rare earth projects and Australia's Arafura Rare Earths secured a government offtake agreement for 500 tonnes per year of NdPr oxide in May 2026, reflecting a diversified Western sourcing strategy that limits any single jurisdiction's leverage.

headline: KINCORA COPPER: 40km MACQUARIE ARC CONFIRMED AT NEVERTIRE NSW — AngloGold JV; 17,620m Drilled; Province-Scale Porphyry System Emerging
snippet: Kincora Copper (ASX: KCC) and JV partner AngloGold Ashanti reported September 22 that 43 drill holes totalling 17,620 metres across the Nevertire South and Nyngan licences in New South Wales have confirmed Macquarie Arc rock continuity across more than 40 kilometres of strike — a fivefold increase relative to the prior drill extent — with copper and gold grades suggestive of proximity to porphyry system centres. Standout hole NEDD011 intersected 312.8 metres of basement, supporting the geological model for a district-scale intrusive-related copper-gold system adjacent to the historic Cobar mining district. Step-out and deeper drilling at the Northern Nevertire Magmatic Complex is the immediate next step, with a 400-square-kilometre gravity survey approximately 27% complete. AngloGold Ashanti's backing as JV partner signals institutional conviction in a porphyry target at a moment when tier-1 copper discoveries are among the most sought-after assets globally.

headline: MIDLAND + SOQUEM HIT 26.8% COPPER, 238 g/t AG IN BOULDERS AT NACHICAPAU QC — Two New Outcrop Showings Found; 4km x 1.5km Labrador Trough Corridor Grows
snippet: Midland Exploration (TSXV: MD) and SOQUEM reported September 22 that the 2026 campaign at the Nachicapau project in Nunavik, Quebec, returned boulder grab samples grading up to 26.8% copper, 0.87 g/t gold and 238 g/t silver from digenite and malachite veins in monzonite dykes — extraordinary surface copper grades within the Labrador Trough, a geological setting known for iron ore but relatively unexplored for copper. Two new vein showings on outcrop added up to 3.03% copper, 0.77 g/t gold and 20.0 g/t silver. The results extend a 4-kilometre by 1.5-kilometre copper-gold-silver corridor identified in discovery work from 2022 to 2025, and the monzonite-dyke host rock is consistent with intrusive-related copper deposits common on the eastern margin of the Canadian Shield — a setting capable of hosting high-tonnage mineralisation if the deeper source intersects favourable stratigraphy.

headline: AUSTRALIAN GOLD AND COPPER: 17m @ 5.3 g/t AU + 163 g/t AG + 17.3% PB+ZN AT EVERGREEN NSW — Second Major Discovery in Two Years; Copper Adds as Third Metal
snippet: Australian Gold and Copper (ASX: AGC) defined a coherent broad zinc-gold-polymetallic system at the Evergreen prospect within its South Cobar project in New South Wales, with highlight hole 26DDBR017 returning 17 metres grading 5.3 g/t gold, 163 g/t silver, 0.8% copper and 17.3% combined lead-zinc — including an 8-metre core at 10.4 g/t gold and 311 g/t silver. Three separate holes additionally returned meaningful copper grades, including 35 metres at 0.5% copper with internal zones at 2.5% copper in hole 26DDBR006, positioning copper as a third distinct growth driver beyond the gold-silver and lead-zinc mineralisation. This marks AGC's second major discovery in two years following Achilles in 2024. An initial Mineral Resource Estimate is targeted once the current 7,000-metre resource definition drilling campaign is complete, with RC assay results from the 21-hole Evergreen program expected in late October to early November 2026.

headline: CANADIAN MINING STOCKS PULLBACK: CONTRARIAN OPPORTUNITY OR MACRO SHIFT? — TSX-V/TSX MINERS DOWN 6-15% FROM AUGUST PEAK; QUALITY JUNIORS APPROACHING INTRINSIC VALUE
snippet: A September 2026 analysis argues that the 6-15% pullback in TSX-V and TSX mining stocks from the August peak represents a classic mid-bull-cycle reset driven by rising Fed rate-hike expectations and dollar strength — not fundamental deterioration. The piece examines enterprise value to resource multiples and identifies several quality Canadian gold and base metal juniors trading below their pre-summer levels despite unchanged project economics, distinguishing between macro-driven pullbacks and project-specific disappointments. The most relevant historical precedent cited is the 2022-2024 rate-hike cycle, in which Canadian mining equities typically bottomed 4-6 weeks before the final rate increase was priced into futures markets — a pattern that, if it holds, would place the current episode near its nadir with a potential October inflection point.

headline: COPPER-SILVER-GOLD TECHNICAL OUTLOOK Q4 2026: $6.40 IS THE FLOOR; $7.00 IS THE BULL TRIGGER — Escondida Vote + Kamoa Restart Timeline Are Key Catalysts
snippet: A late September technical analysis of copper, silver and gold sets out the key Q4 2026 levels: copper at $6.40 per pound as the line-in-sand for the intermediate bull case, with $7.00 as the trigger for a fresh bullish leg if the Escondida strike vote fails and BHP's restart extends beyond October. The analysis notes copper's 16% year-to-date gain and proximity to the September 8 record of $6.83 despite the current macro headwind from a stronger dollar, arguing the underlying supply deficit thesis remains intact. Silver's technical picture is described as the most complex of the three, with the January $121 peak acting as a significant overhang and the $60 level identified as critical support; gold's 150-day moving average stays declining with the metal printing lower highs and lower lows since the January record — a bearish short-term pattern that the analysis argues will persist until October Fed hike expectations reverse.

headline: FALLING METALS PRICES DRAG CANADIAN MINERS LOWER — MOTLEY FOOL CANADA IDENTIFIES ROYALTY STREAMERS AS MOST INSULATED; SELECTIVITY KEY IN RATE-HIKE ENVIRONMENT
snippet: A Motley Fool Canada analysis published September 23 examines why Canadian gold and base metals mining stocks are underperforming despite historically elevated commodity prices, attributing the divergence to the dollar's two-month high and re-pricing of the October Fed hike compressing equity valuations across gold, copper and silver simultaneously. The piece argues that the unusual co-movement of multiple commodity headwinds makes broad mining index buying less effective than individual stock selection, and identifies royalty and streaming companies as the category most insulated from the current pullback given their fixed-cost exposure and volume rather than margin leverage. For retail investors managing TSXV positions, the analysis offers a framework for distinguishing stocks under macro pressure from those facing project-specific disappointment — arguing only the former group is likely to recover sharply when rate-hike expectations peak.
